title: Sentence Structure, Part 1
sourceNote: The auto-captions are heavily garbled; the sentences were reconstructed from context and the teacher's explanation.
objectives: I can find the subject and the verb in a simple sentence
I can place the verb in second position in statements
I can build W-questions with the verb in second position
I can build yes/no questions with the verb in first position

grammar.title: Subject and verb
grammar.body: Every sentence needs a **subject** (who does something) and a **verb** (the action or state). The subject decides how the verb is conjugated, so the verb changes its ending: *ich heiße*, but *du heißt*. You will study conjugation in detail in the next lessons.

grammar.title: Statements: the verb is in position 2
grammar.body: The most important rule of German word order: in a statement the conjugated verb is always the **second element**. The subject can stand before the verb or after it. Only the position of the verb stays fixed.
grammar.ar: الفعل المصرّف يأتي دائمًا في المرتبة الثانية في الجملة الخبرية.

examples.en: Verb still second; the subject comes after it.

grammar.title: W-questions: the verb is in position 2
grammar.body: Questions that start with a W-word (*wie, was, wo, woher …*) are called **W-Fragen**. The W-word is in position 1, the verb in position 2 and the subject follows the verb.

examples.en: What is your name? (verb: heißen, subject: Sie)
Where do you come from? (verb: kommst, subject: du)

grammar.title: Yes/no questions: the verb is in position 1
grammar.body: Questions that can be answered with *ja* or *nein* are **Ja/Nein-Fragen**. This is the exception: the conjugated verb is in **first position** and the subject follows directly.
grammar.ar: في أسئلة (نعم/لا) يأتي الفعل في المرتبة الأولى.

mistakes.why: The verb must stay in second position.
A yes/no question starts with the verb.
In W-questions the verb is in second position.

lines.de: Hallo! Ich heiße Anna. Wie heißen Sie?
lines.en: Hello! My name is Anna. What is your name?

lines.de: Ich heiße Tom. Woher kommen Sie?
lines.en: My name is Tom. Where do you come from?

lines.de: Ich komme aus Deutschland. Kommen Sie aus England?
lines.en: I come from Germany. Do you come from England?

lines.de: Ja, ich komme aus England. Wo wohnen Sie?
lines.en: Yes, I come from England. Where do you live?

tip: Say the sentence aloud and count the elements: the verb must always be the second one in a statement or a W-question.

comprehension.q: In which position is the verb in a statement?
In which position is the verb in a yes/no question?
What is the verb and what is the subject in *Woher kommst du?*
What are questions that start with wie, was or wo called?

exercises.title: Word order
exercises.instructions: Put the words in the correct order. Start statements with the subject.

exercises.title: Find the verb and the subject
exercises.instructions: Write the verb or the subject as asked.

items.q: Ich bin Marie. Which word is the verb?
Wie heißen Sie? Which word is the subject?
Kommst du aus Italien? Which word is the verb?
Wo wohnen Sie? Which word is the subject?
Sprechen Sie Italienisch? Which word is the verb?
Heute bin ich in Berlin. Which word is the subject?

items.expl: It can be answered with ja or nein.

summary: A sentence needs a subject and a conjugated verb; the subject decides the verb form.
In statements the verb is in second position; the subject can stand before or after it.
W-questions (wie, was, wo, woher …): W-word, verb, subject.
Yes/no questions: the verb is in first position, followed by the subject.
